1840: The agent said the flight was boarding from the back, and you were, of course, seated in the middle.
1841: You measured the legroom with your knees, found the exact spot where they touched the seat ahead, and accepted it.
1842: They reached your row and announced they'd run out of the good meal, leaving you the mysterious other one.
1843: You visited the little room at the back of the plane, where everything was within reach at exactly the same time.
1844: You plugged your headphones into the armrest, and one ear worked, the other offered only distant whispers.
1845: The captain said something warm and important over the speaker, and you caught roughly one word of it.
1846: You reached your row, checked the number twice, and lowered yourself in like you'd earned the whole seat.
1847: The plane wobbled once, firmly, and everyone kept reading while gripping their armrests harder.
1848: Your elbow found the call button by accident, and a crew member arrived, kind and expectant, for nothing.
1849: The seat-back screen offered a hundred choices, and you spent the first hour choosing instead of watching.
1850: Two armrests, three people, and one unspoken agreement nobody remembers making. You lost it early.
1851: You asked for water, got a cup with a single brave ice cube, and thanked the crew like they'd saved you.
1852: The armrest between you fit exactly one elbow, and it had clearly already made its decision without you.
1853: You drew the middle seat, the one spot on the plane designed by someone who has never sat in it.
1854: You unfolded the thin blanket they gave you, and it covered either your shoulders or your knees, never both.
1855: You hung your coat somewhere confidently, and spent the rest of the flight not quite sure it still existed.
1856: Your seatmate told you their entire life story, and honestly, some of it was pretty good.
1857: The person beside you asked what you do, answered for you, then agreed with themselves warmly.
1858: Your neighbor watched the little map the whole flight, narrating the plane's progress to absolutely no one.
1859: The chatty passenger beside you paused exactly once, to breathe, and you almost escaped. Almost.
1860: Your seatmate wanted to show you photos. All of them. You now feel very close to their garden.
1861: The person beside you fell asleep before takeoff and stayed there, peaceful, while you did the worrying.
1862: Your neighbor slept the whole flight, sturdy and still, like a passenger-shaped piece of furniture.
1863: You closed your eyes to nap, and your brain chose that exact moment to review everything you'd ever said.
1864: Your seatmate slept with the deep confidence of someone who is definitely not solving a case.
1865: Your seat reclined a proud half-inch and then refused, on principle, to go any farther.
1866: Your phone hit two percent right as the good part began, and you watched it decide your evening for you.
1867: The person behind you tapped your seat in a slow, thoughtful rhythm, composing something only they could hear.
1868: A stranger asked to swap seats so their family could sit together, so now you're somewhere new. Fine.
1869: You pulled the seatbelt to fit and discovered the previous passenger was apparently shaped nothing like you.
1870: Someone was in your seat, apologized, and moved, and for one bright moment the whole system worked.
1871: You stepped onto the moving walkway and instantly felt like the fastest, laziest person in the building.
1872: You took the aisle, which means standing politely every time anyone else remembers they have legs.
1873: Your neighbor unpacked a small home onto the tray table: a book, a snack, a blanket, a whole routine.
1874: Your neighbor unwrapped a snack of great personality, and the whole row quietly learned what it was.
1875: You got the window seat, which is lovely, and also a quiet promise never to need the bathroom.
1876: The passenger beside you offered you a mint, unprompted, and it slightly restored your faith in flights.
1877: Your seatmate woke up, checked that you were still there, and went right back to sleep. Reassuring.
1878: You and your seatmate exchanged one polite hello, then honored a beautiful, hours-long silence together.
1879: Your neighbor did a crossword the whole flight and never once asked you for a single answer. Impressive.
